generated_by: feasibility research pass; every value below reconciled against the Q2 2026 figures in ai_capex_forward_roic_analysis_v02_methodology.md

next_refresh.note: MSFT quarter end coincides with the calendar quarter (2026-09-30, its FY27 Q1). ORCL does NOT: its FY27 Q1 ends 2026-08-31 and is mapped into the CY2026Q3 bucket one month early.

tiers.auto: A single XBRL fact, uniquely identified by concept + period + dimensional context, verified to equal the model's figure. No arithmetic.
tiers.derived: Arithmetic over two or more verified XBRL facts (almost always year-to-date differencing).
tiers.manual: The figure does not exist as an XBRL fact in any SEC filing. A human must read a transcript, webcast, or slide deck.

access.companyfacts: Obtainable from https://data.sec.gov/api/xbrl/companyfacts/CIK##########.json (or companyconcept). Undimensioned facts only.
access.inline_xbrl_dimensional: The fact EXISTS in XBRL but carries a dimensional qualifier. The companyfacts/companyconcept APIs strip dimensions and will NOT return it. Must parse ix:nonFraction elements out of the filing's primary inline-XBRL document and resolve xbrli:context segments.
access.not_in_xbrl: No XBRL fact anywhere in the SEC filings.

conventions.critical_warning: Two of the five demand facts (MSFT, AMZN) are access=inline_xbrl_dimensional. For MSFT, blindly calling companyfacts for us-gaap:RevenueRemainingPerformanceObligation returns 684000000000 (TOTAL company RPO) instead of the 678000000000 commercial RPO the model uses. That is a silent 0.9% error, not a fetch failure. Any fetcher MUST branch on the `access` field.
conventions.unit: All monetary values USD, unscaled (a value of 44924000000 means $44.924B).
conventions.verification_note: `verified_q2_2026` is the value this mapping reproduced from live SEC data on 2026-08-31; `model_q2_2026` is the value the methodology doc reports. They are equal for every fact except MSFT capex (see that entry).

best_xbrl_proxy.status: APPROXIMATION, NOT AN IDENTITY. Microsoft has never published a reconciliation between its management capex metric and these two GAAP tags. Microsoft's IR event page states the $41B comprises ~$35.8B cash plus a finance-lease component; one secondary source puts that component at $5.6B, which does not sum to $41.0B given a $35.8B cash base. The composition is therefore UNVERIFIED and the proxy must not be trusted to the reported figure's precision.

META.name: Meta Platforms, Inc.
META.offset_note: Fiscal year is the calendar year. Calendar Q2 2026 = FY2026 Q2.

demand_fact.label: Quarterly revenue
demand_fact.derivation: single fact; Meta tags standalone 3-month INCOME-STATEMENT durations (unlike its cash-flow items), so no differencing is needed
demand_fact.companyfacts_path: facts['us-gaap']['RevenueFromContractWithCustomerExcludingAssessedTax']['units']['USD'] where start == quarter_start and end == period_end
demand_fact.note: META is the only company whose demand fact is a revenue figure rather than a backlog/RPO measure - Meta discloses no RPO. This makes it the easiest of the five and also the least comparable: it is a realized flow, not a contracted stock.

capex_fact.label: Capital expenditures INCLUDING principal payments on finance leases
capex_fact.why_derived: Two components, and Meta's 10-Q cash flow statement presents YEAR-TO-DATE columns only, so each component needs YTD differencing. Q1 needs no differencing; Q2/Q3/Q4 always do.
capex_fact.component_note: Meta's definition uses finance-lease PRINCIPAL PAYMENTS (us-gaap:FinanceLeasePrincipalPayments, a financing-activity cash outflow). This is NOT the same as finance-lease ROU asset additions (us-gaap:RightOfUseAssetObtainedInExchangeForFinanceLeaseLiability), which is what Microsoft's management metric appears to use. Do not share one formula across the two companies.
capex_fact.cross_check: 8-K Exhibit 99.1: 'Capital expenditures, including principal payments on finance leases, were $31.08 billion.' The XBRL derivation ($31.078B) is MORE precise than the press release's rounded $31.08B.

annual_denominator.label: FY2026 capital expenditure outlook range midpoint
annual_denominator.not_machine_readable_reason: NOT MACHINE-READABLE AS XBRL, but it IS present as prose in the SEC-filed 8-K Exhibit 99.1 (unlike MSFT/GOOG/AMZN, whose outlooks are call-only). It is untagged text, so extraction is regex-fragile.
annual_denominator.prose_location: 8-K Exhibit 99.1, CFO Outlook section: 'We anticipate 2026 capital expenditures, including principal payments on finance leases, to be in the range of $130-145 billion, narrowed from our prior outlook of $125-145 billion.'
annual_denominator.regex_trap: The SAME SENTENCE contains the PRIOR outlook ($125-145 billion). A naive 'first range after the phrase capital expenditures' regex is only correct by luck of word order; a 'last range in the sentence' regex would grab the superseded figure.
